results.corrected_extracted: Stated limitations: the cause of death determined by the assigned forensic pathologist was assumed correct; illicit drugs present at death were taken as at least contributing except in deaths with class I natural or traumatic processes; the sample reflects western North Carolina only. In the Conclusions the authors call the almost 10% false-positive rate a significant number of cases that could have been misclassified, while describing the study as informational and its data as not meant to sway offices toward one practice.
results.note: Limitations confirmed (p. 192, Discussion 5th paragraph). The Conclusions call the almost-10% rate a significant number that could have been misclassified; 'informational, not meant to sway' describes the study and its data, not the rate.
Checked p. 544, Figure 2 (300 dpi), p. 545 and Table 3 note: 64.7%, 80%, 715/1,326 = 53.9%, 674/709 = 95.1% recomputed. Shares of offices, not deaths; 80% is quoted from the BJS report.
